title: Merge Triplets to Form Target Triplet
spaceBreakdown:
- bool p0, p1, p2: three scalars → O(1)
- loop variable t (reference, no copy): O(1)
- not counted: input triplets, target
approach: The max operation only increases values, so any triplet with a value exceeding the target in any position can never participate in a valid merge. Among the remaining triplets (all values ≤ target), we just need each of the three target positions to be matched by at least one such triplet. We scan once, tracking three booleans for whether each position has been hit.
hints: The merge operation takes element-wise maxima, so values can only grow. Which triplets could ever be safely used without pushing some position past the target?

Greedy single-pass filter: keep only triplets whose every value is ≤ target, and track which of the three target positions are matched. In Example 1, [2,5,3] matches position 0 and [1,7,5] matches positions 1 and 2, so all three are covered → true.

```
p0 = p1 = p2 = false
for each triplet t:
    if t[0] <= target[0] and t[1] <= target[1] and t[2] <= target[2]:
        if t[0] == target[0]: p0 = true
        if t[1] == target[1]: p1 = true
        if t[2] == target[2]: p2 = true
return p0 and p1 and p2
```

**Overshoot in one position** - a triplet matches target in two positions but exceeds it in the third
`Input: triplets = [[2,8,5]], target = [2,7,5]` → `Expected: false`
⚠️ Bug: checking each position independently without the all-values-≤-target filter → returns `true`

**Single triplet** - n = 1, the triplet already equals the target
`Input: triplets = [[2,7,5]], target = [2,7,5]` → `Expected: true`
⚠️ Bug: requiring at least two triplets before returning true → returns `false`

**All valid, none matching** - every triplet has all values ≤ target but none equals any target value
`Input: triplets = [[1,1,1],[2,2,2]], target = [3,3,3]` → `Expected: false`
⚠️ Bug: returning true whenever any valid triplet exists → returns `true`

**Partial coverage** - two of three positions matched, the third never appears
`Input: triplets = [[2,5,3],[1,7,4]], target = [2,7,5]` → `Expected: false`
⚠️ Bug: only checking two of the three position flags → returns `true`

followUps.q: What if the merge operation used min instead of max?
followUps.a: Flip the filter: keep only triplets whose every value is ≥ target, then check that each position is matched by at least one such triplet. Still O(n) time and O(1) space.

followUps.q: What if each triplet had k elements instead of 3?
followUps.a: Use a boolean array of size k instead of three scalars, applying the same filter-and-match logic per position. O(n·k) time, O(k) space.

followUps.q: What if triplets arrive as a stream and cannot all be stored?
followUps.a: Process each triplet on arrival, updating the position flags in place. O(1) space per element, single pass, same O(n) total time.
